best_for: Gamers, study groups and online communities who hang out in voice channels and text chat and want Discord in its own window on the desktop.

points.title: Free app, paid extras
points.text: The desktop app costs nothing to download, and Discord's paid plan, Nitro, is optional. Nitro mostly changes limits and looks, such as upload size, stream quality, emoji and profiles.

points.title: Nitro is the paid layer
points.text: Nitro Basic is USD 2.99 a month and raises the upload limit to 50 MB, with custom emoji anywhere. Nitro is USD 9.99 a month, with uploads up to 1 GB, HD streaming and custom profiles. Prices were read on the date below.

points.title: Try features early
points.text: Discord offers a Public Test Build (PTB) for Windows, Mac and Linux that gets new features before they reach the main app. It is a separate download from Discord's site.

points.title: Linux Flatpak has sandbox limits
points.text: The Flatpak is verified on Flathub, so it comes from Discord Inc. Its sandbox stops game activity, Rich Presence and unrestricted file access from working out of the box, and it is x64 only. Discord also offers .deb, RPM, tar.gz and Arch packages on its own site.

points.title: Same account on every screen
points.text: Besides the desktop apps, Discord runs on iOS, Android and Meta Quest, and links to PlayStation and Xbox accounts, so one account works from PC to phone to console.

points.title: Installs and updates
points.text: The Windows installer listed here is x64 and installs for the current user, no admin rights needed; Discord's own site also has an Arm64 build. The Mac build is universal and needs macOS 13 or later. The Windows listing keeps 155 versions; macOS and Linux list only the current release, so downgrades there need another source.
